title: Union Bank of India - 532477 - Union Bank Of India Informed The Exchanges About Transcript Of Post Earnings Call Held On 15-07-2026

read.thesis: Union Bank's Q1 FY27 call stresses CASA/RTD stability and NIM defence at 2.80%, but credit growth is soft, bulk deposits are being shed, and ECL transition (about INR11,300 crore) remains unquantified on run-rate.

summary.headline: Union Bank of India Q1 FY27: CASA+RTD averaged ~INR41,000 crore, bulk deposits shed ~INR18,000-20,000 crore, cost of deposits down 18 bps, NIM 2.80%.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a quarter of record operating profit (INR8,003 crore) and ROA of 1.36%, with NIM up to 2.80% from 2.64% last quarter. The bank shed bulk deposits and kept CASA and retail term deposits as the priority, which lowered cost of deposits by 18 bps while credit growth lagged the system. Management took an additional INR100 crore of provisions in the quarter, taking its own ECL buffer to INR800 crore, and wrote off more than last quarter. Management estimated the total ECL requirement at about INR11,300 crore, with about INR5,500 crore already carried, and said the remaining INR6,000 crore is not required immediately.

financial_highlights.change: Maintained for last three quarters per management
Up from 2.64% in the previous quarter

financial_highlights.metric: Bulk deposit share of total deposits

financial_highlights.change: INR562 crore in Q4 FY26; INR14 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: About INR630-640 crore in last two quarters

financial_highlights.change: Down about INR438 crore from about -INR800 crore last quarter
From INR420 crore in March quarter (as cited by analyst)
Sanctioned about INR12,000 crore; expected total INR14,000-15,000 crore

segments.name: Retail and CASA deposits
segments.commentary: Average CASA about INR24,000 crore and RTD about INR17,000 crore; management cited 95-99% stickiness in savings and current balances. NACH registrations rose from 12,000-13,000 a day to 18,000.

segments.name: Agriculture and SMF (PSLC)
segments.commentary: PSLC income of INR217 crore booked in Q1 FY27 against nil a year earlier. Management said the full-year level depends on SMF growth, but did not give a number for the year.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book fell by about INR2,500-3,000 crore as the bank made compliance changes. Management said it is rebuilding the book under regulatory norms.

segments.name: Foreign branches
segments.commentary: Yield on global advances at 7.90%, with down-selling of syndicated loans at 100-140 bps spreads, which limits yield gains.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth aim at industry plus about 1%; management said advances growth of 12-13% or more is expected with the sanctioned-not-disbursed corporate pipeline above INR1 lakh crore.
Deposit growth expected to be around 2% in the near term; management said bulk deposits will be taken only when needed after CASA and RTD.
NIM aim is to improve from 2.80% after defending it; management said it has bottomed.
FCNR (B) mobilisation target of USD1.5-2 billion (about INR20,000 crore) by September 2026; so far USD106 million; OFCB plan of USD200-300 million.

ECL: total requirement about INR11,300 crore, with about INR5,500 crore carried including INR800 crore additional buffer, leaving about INR6,000 crore to be provided by 31 March 2027. Model built with EY and Oracle; the impact is one-time plus a monthly ongoing component.
Tier 2 bonds: INR850 crore called in Q1 and about INR2,500 crore to be called; blended cost of the bonds cited as 8.7%.
capex_capacity: Ecosystem banking vertical with about 1,200 staff, 118 centres and 12 hubs was set up to focus on relationship management and deposit sourcing.
Management has not announced capex or branch-expansion plans in the call.
Recoveries were about INR750 crore in Q1; management expects INR4,500-5,000 crore for FY27 on that run-rate.
demand_pricing: Average domestic advances yield 8.01% and global yield 7.90%; the prior-quarter domestic yield was not disclosed on the call.
Domestic corporate mix at about 57:43 (retail/MSME vs corporate); management said IBPC is not bought and that IBPC was sold in Q1.
Management underwrote INR60,000-70,000 crore of corporate loans in the past eight to nine months and is down-selling them.
Stress in MSME is seen in low-value tickets, mostly state-scheme and guarantee-covered; an MSME study covered 2,500-plus customers across 140 regional offices.
Management attributed the weak credit growth to ECLGS disbursements reducing cash-credit balances, not to stress in borrowers.

qa_highlights.question: When will deposit growth pick up to bridge the gap with loan growth, and how much FCNR can the bank mobilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bulk deposits were shed while CASA and RTD were prioritised. It targets USD1.5-2 billion of FCNR by September, about INR20,000 crore, with USD106 million done so far.

qa_highlights.question: Why did recoveries fall and provisions rise, and is there MSME stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries were lower because Q4 included a large Supreme Court-linked recovery; management said Q1 recoveries exceed slippages. It acknowledged MSME stress in low-value tickets and attributed the ECLGS-driven CC reduction to customers keeping cash.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the cost-of-funds steadiness, and what is the outlook for Tier 2 bonds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said high-cost Tier 2 bonds were called, INR850 crore in Q1 and about INR2,500 crore further, at a blended 8.7%, which should reduce the cost of funds going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL annual run-rate and what is the remaining provisioning need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-time ECL requirement is about INR11,300 crore against INR5,500 crore carried, with about INR6,000 crore left. Management did not give an ongoing annual credit-cost figure; an analyst estimated a CRAR hit to 17.54% if absorbed in year one.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic and global yields on advances fall, and what drives NIM expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic yield on advances was 8.01% and global yield 7.90%. Management expects yields to bottom out, with NIM gains from converting lower-yield book and from funding cost declines.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the LCR change and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the LCR benefit was a net 2.5-3% (about INR4,500 crore), from a reduced run-off factor on society/trust AOPs (100% to 40%) and deposit-mix changes.

risks_watch: CD ratio at 85-86%, which management said is the upper comfortable limit; deposit growth at about 2% against credit growth of 12-13% or more.
ECL provisioning of about INR6,000 crore still to be provided by 31 March 2027; quarterly ECL run-rate not yet quantified.
MSME stress from West Asia and macro conditions, with ECLGS disbursements of about INR10,000 crore of INR12,000 crore sanctioned.
SMA 2 bucket rose by about INR350 crore per an analyst; gross slippages reported as flat quarter on quarter.
Treasury and tax-refund income fell from INR1,439 crore (Q1 FY26) to a run-rate of about INR630-640 crore plus INR532 crore of tax-refund income.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, asset quality and capital; more guarded on credit and deposit growth, where management gave no timeline for closing the gap with the system. Management often deflected specifics (ECL run-rate, Q1 FY26 domestic yield, bank-wide SMA) to follow-up.
key_quotes: So even now, I would not like to give figures, but even today our average CASA figures are better than the June 30th CASA figures because that is what I am saying about the about the vertical which we have created.
So we are very sure that not only 11% to 12% or 14%, but we aim to move better than 18% to 20% in these three sectors going forward.
IBPC, we do not want to even hear it.

growth.why: Management aims for advances growth of industry plus 1% (cited as 12-13% or more) backed by a sanctioned-not-disbursed corporate pipeline above INR1 lakh crore, and FCNR(B) mobilisation of USD1.5-2 billion by September 2026, but no new capacity, capex or branch expansion was announced; quarterly revenue and EBITDA growth YoY were not stated.
